title: bug: the Publish card's Resolve control is refused 403 from the owner's paired browser, so a stuck UNKNOWN publish still has no exit the owner can reach
description:
Found by worker-952c612b on parent task-21be6e9055984413a651ce6ee331e2c8 (step 1, measured in step 2).

THE GAP. The owner's browser authenticates as a paired session: session-authenticator.ts:139 sets principal = sessionId, a durable HUMAN. repository.publish_resolve is operator-only and fences itself (publish-resolve-command.ts:39). It is NOT among the paired-human widenings at daemon-command-registry.ts:441-445, although its sibling repository.publish is. affordance-read.ts still offers it to every reader.

THE EFFECT. A Resolve click answers 403 OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED@DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION with "this command requires the configured operator principal". This is pinned, with a production pairing mint, by the paired-browser dispatch in apps/daemon/src/repository/publish-resolve-journey.test.ts. No other surface reaches the operator principal either:
- the moe CLI's KNOWN_COMMANDS has no resolve command;
- `moe mcp --as-operator` classifies the kind MCP_NEVER_DELEGATED.

THE FIX needs an OWNER ruling. The candidate is to admit a paired durable HUMAN holding ADMIN, on the pattern of release.decide's releaseByPairedAdmin (release-decide-command.ts:77) or goal.cancel's pairedHumanKind, with MCP exclusion unchanged. The fix then flips the journey's paired-browser arm to ACCEPTED.
definitionOfDone: An owner ruling on the widening is recorded on this row before any code changes.

If widened: a paired durable HUMAN holding ADMIN resolves an UNKNOWN publish through the production registry, and publish-resolve-journey.test.ts's paired-browser arm asserts ACCEPTED. A paired HUMAN without ADMIN, and an agent session, are still refused 403 OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED@DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION, each asserted with its code, layer and detail. The kind stays in MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS and MCP_NEVER_DELEGATED_KINDS.
